turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
High-efficiency cells in the training set are almost exclusively 3D Pb mixed-cation absorbers (FAMAPbI, FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI) with a ~1.5–1.6 eV gap. Lead-free, Sn, Bi and wide-gap Br/Cl compositions sit far lower because of defect density, oxidation and optical mismatch. The same data show that interface recombination, not bulk absorption, sets the top of the distribution: 2D ammonium capping layers and SAMs push medians to 20–23 %, while otherwise identical stacks without passivation sit at 17–19.5 %.

Selective contacts follow the same pattern. In n-i-p, SnO2 (or compact/mesoporous TiO2) aligned to the perovskite CBM, Li-doped Spiro-MeOTAD (HOMO ~ –5.2 eV) and Au give the highest Voc and FF; Ag without a MoOx interlayer is inferior because of halide corrosion. In p-i-n, PTAA (or PTAA/PFN-Br) plus a fullerene/BCP bilayer and Cu/Ag is reproducibly 18–20.5 %; PEDOT:PSS, carbon and missing BCP all increase recombination or series resistance. Multi-step spin-coating improves film compactness relative to single-step or non-spin processes; flexible substrates and exotic oxides (ZnO, Cr2O3, Nb2O5) are modest penalties.

Applying those constraints to the pool:

- c015 is a CsFAMAPbBrI / (EPA)PbI 2D–3D bilayer on the classic TiO2-c|mp / Spiro / Au stack—the exact architecture that produced the 22.9 % and 19.7 % training medians. EPA (like OA, PEA, CH3O-PEIA) passivates the HTL interface and is the single strongest positive feature in the data.
- c085 and c093 are inverted CsFAMAPbBrI cells with PTAA, a fullerene/BCP electron stack and Cu or Ag. They match the 20.1–20.3 % training recipes; PFN-Br on c085 further improves wetting and contact selectivity, so it ranks above c093.
- c092 is FAMAPbI (optimal gap) on SnO2-np / Spiro / MoOx|Ag with a double spin-coat—the closest analogue is the 19.5 % FAMAPbBrI cell, and both the lower-gap absorber and the MoOx barrier are upgrades.
- c008 is the same FAMAPbI absorber in the planar SnO2-c / Spiro / Au n-i-p geometry that already reached 19.8 % (TiO2-c) and 20.2 % (FAPbI / SnO2-np) in training; double spin-coating further favours a compact film.

All other pool entries are missing at least one of these ingredients (wrong absorber, PEDOT:PSS, carbon, no passivation, flexible foil, or a poorly aligned HTL) and are therefore expected to lie lower.

Final: c015, c085, c093, c092, c008
